2027-01-04.title: Monday after the Second Sunday after Yaldo · Prophet Malachi; St Kuriakose Elias Chavara
readings: Without faith it is impossible to please God
2027-01-04.alt: Season of Yaldo and Denho. The feast of Denho is on Wednesday: remind the faithful.
2027-01-04.verse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
theo: Hebrews begins its great chapter on faith with three ancient figures. Abel offered a more acceptable sacrifice; Enoch “pleased God” and was taken up; Noah, warned of things not yet seen, built an ark and saved his household. The principle is simple: “without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.” Faith is not a feeling but a life that trusts God's word and acts on it.

The Gospel gives the Beatitudes, the portrait of a life of faith: poor in spirit, mourning, meek, hungry for righteousness, merciful, pure in heart, peacemakers, persecuted. Today we remember the prophet Malachi, last of the prophets, who promised that “the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings”, and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, a son of Kerala who lived the Beatitudes as priest, founder and teacher. Two days before Denho, they point us to the Sun that rises at the Jordan.

2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, Sun of righteousness, you taught us the Beatitudes and lived them perfectly. Through the prayers of the prophet Malachi and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, give us a pure heart and a living faith, so that we may see God. Amen.
altar: The pure in heart will see God. In the Holy Qurbono we see him already under the veil of bread and wine; purity of heart prepares us to receive him.

family.explain: Jesus taught on a mountain: blessed are the gentle, the merciful, the peacemakers. God makes them truly happy.
family.intention: We pray that our family may be peacemakers.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of these blessings would you like to live this week?”

illus: When St Chavara saw that poor children in Kerala had no schools, he did not write complaints; he opened schools beside churches and even arranged midday meals so that poor children would come. Meekness and hunger for righteousness became a school bell.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went up the mountain and taught the Beatitudes. Teach us now, and give us pure hearts. Amen.
share: Without faith it is impossible to please God (Hebrews 11:6). How do I show my faith in deeds?
Blessed are the pure in heart (Matthew 5:8). What clouds my heart?
St Chavara lived the Beatitudes in Kerala. Which saint of our land inspires me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us blessed in your ways.
interc: For the Church in Kerala, that she may be rich in saints.
For teachers and schools, through St Chavara.
For the poor in spirit and those who mourn.
For peacemakers in our families and society.
For our group, that we may prepare well for Denho.
pm.close: Father, you raised up prophets and saints to prepare the way of your Son. Give us faith that pleases you and hearts pure enough to see you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews 11 is the great hall of faith. Today we hear about the first three heroes. Abel offered God a more acceptable sacrifice. Enoch pleased God and was taken up. Noah, warned about things not yet seen, built an ark and saved his household (Hebrews 11:4–7).

The key sentence is this: without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him (Hebrews 11:6). Faith is trusting God's word enough to build an ark before the rain.

In the Gospel Jesus goes up the mountain and gives the Beatitudes. They are the portrait of a person of faith: poor in spirit, merciful, pure in heart, a peacemaker. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God (Matthew 5:8).

Today we remember the prophet Malachi, who promised that the sun of righteousness would rise with healing in its wings (Malachi 4:2), and St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, who lived the Beatitudes among the poor of Kerala, building schools and homes of prayer.
On Wednesday we celebrate Denho, when that Sun rises at the Jordan. Let us choose one Beatitude to live this week, and prepare our hearts to see God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: happy are the kind, the gentle and the peacemakers! Choose one this week. Will you be a peacemaker at home?

intro: Theme: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.”
Faith that pleases God, the Beatitudes, and the rising Sun.

q: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.
And without faith it is impossible to please God, for whoever would approach him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.
points.apply: Act today on one word of God you have been postponing.

points.h: Blessed are the pure in heart
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

sub: The Sun rises at the Jordan.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings. You shall go out leaping like calves from the stall.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hid.
points.apply: Light a lamp at home for Denho.

concl: Faith, purity of heart and light belong together.
The Sun of righteousness is about to rise at the Jordan.
